text:
[LERR.1.4.12] **A fault raised while matching reaches a surface once per
derivation of its pair.** A join test answers a pair: a token in the node's left
memory and a candidate fact in its right memory ([IRET.7.6]). A pair is **live**
while both are there. An assertion or a retraction of a fact, with the
propagation it causes, **derives** the pairs that are live after it and were not
live before it, the pairs below a negated pattern it releases included
([IRET.7.9.3]).

For a `TypeError` or a `ComputationError`, the engine **must** record the fault a
pair's tests yield ([LERR.1.4.11]) for each pair the operation derives, and for
no other pair. A pair the engine evaluates that is not live when the operation
completes, and a pair the operation ends, record nothing, whatever their tests
yield. A pair that ends and is later derived again records again.

The engine **must** record the faults one operation derives once its
propagation has completed, ordered by:

1. the terminal ordinal of the rule the node belongs to ([LDET.5.4],
   [LDET.5.10]);
2. the pair's facts, as [LDET.5.5] orders a rule's matches: the token's facts
   and then the candidate, pattern by pattern, each ranked by when it entered
   working memory;
3. the node's position in the rule's chain, the shallower first.

Which faults one operation records, and their order, are therefore a function of
working memory before and after it. How the engine traverses its memories,
whether it indexes a join, and the order in which it visits alpha memories
**must not** change them ([LDET.5.9]).

An `EngineError` raised while matching halts the tier where it is raised
([IRET.9.6]); a run that raises one is outside the determinism guarantee
([LDET.1.11]).

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__a1
idris.note: A fixture: `a1`, kind 0, key 7.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__append_same_set
idris.note: Appending respects membership on both sides.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__b1
idris.note: A fixture: `b1`, kind 1, key 7, payload 1.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__chain_live_of
idris.note: A chain's live pairs recomputed from the program and working memory: each node's front against its alpha's view of working memory, the front advanced by the node's own propagation. Reads no memory of the network.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__chain_live_recomputed
idris.note: A consistent chain's live pairs are the recompute's, node by node: the left memory is the front it receives, as a set, and the right memory the alpha's view of working memory.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__chain_pair_in_wm
idris.note: A live pair of the recompute is over live facts: the token's and the candidate.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__cross_same_set
idris.note: Two fronts with the same members pair alike with one memory.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__derived
idris.note: THE DERIVED PAIRS of a state change, the clause's 'derives': live after, not before, over the network's live pairs -- the pairs below a released negated pattern included, since a released token's pairs are live after. What a match-time TypeError or ComputationError is recorded for, once per derivation.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__evaluated_pairs_vary_with_alpha_order_derived_do_not
idris.note: The two alpha orders evaluate different transients and derive the same nothing: no alpha order makes the evaluated pairs the derived ones, and the clause's record over derived pairs does not see the order ([LDET.5.9]). Computed.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__front_in_wm
idris.note: A node's propagation keeps a front's facts live: a `no` node filters the front, a positive node extends its tokens by candidates of the alpha's view of working memory.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__key_eq
idris.note: A fixture: two keys compared, decided.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__live_is_a_function_of_wm
idris.note: (b) THE LIVE PAIRS ARE A FUNCTION OF WORKING MEMORY: under the view a network's live pairs are, as a set, their recompute from the program and working memory. The derived pairs are the filter of the recompute after by the recompute before, so which pairs an operation derives -- and which faults it records -- is a function of working memory before and after it, whatever the engine's traversal, index or alpha order ([LDET.5.9]). Sets, not lists: the order of one operation's records, the clause's three keys, is not modelled.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__net_live_of
idris.note: The live pairs of a network recomputed from its working memory, chain by chain.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__net_pair_in_wm
idris.note: Over every chain, from the empty token.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__per_chain_recomputed
idris.note: Chain by chain, with the rule ordinals.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__retraction_derives_no_pair_of_its_fact
idris.note: (c) A RETRACTION DERIVES NO PAIR CONTAINING ITS FACT: a pair derived by retracting `f` is live after, so its facts are in the working memory after, from which `f` is gone. The pairs a retraction ends record nothing, whatever the engine evaluates on the way.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__retraction_evaluates_but_derives_not_its_fact
idris.note: A retraction of `b1` evaluates a pair containing `b1` -- the released `(a1)`'s wave meets `b1` in the second alpha before dispatch reaches it -- and derives no such pair: (c) at an instance, a trap the clause does not record. Computed.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__rule
idris.note: A fixture: `A a, no B b where b.k == a.k, B c where <traps>` over two alpha indices.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__same_key
idris.note: A fixture: the `no` pattern's test.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__same_key_of
idris.note: A fixture: `b.k == a.k` over the token's one fact.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__shared
idris.note: A fixture: one `B` alpha shared by both patterns ([IRET.6.6]).

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__split
idris.note: A fixture: a second `B` alpha for `c`, after the `no` pattern's.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__split_other
idris.note: A fixture: the same two alphas the other way round.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__transient_pair_records_nothing
idris.note: TRANSIENT ON ASSERT RECORDS NOTHING: with `a1` live, asserting `b1` evaluates `((a1), b1)` at the trapping `c` node and then blocks `(a1)`; the pair is live neither before nor after and is not derived, so the clause records no trap. Computed; the lockstep scenario 113_transient_trap and the vector logical/LERR.1.4.12_transient_pair_records_nothing run it against both runtimes.

idris.name: lerr_1_4_12__traps
idris.note: A fixture: `c`'s test, a trap on every pair.
